review_notes: No Day 7 resource pack is supplied - these thresholds are developer-authored and self-reviewed against real, measured pipeline output (the real GroundedAnswerService, real input policy, real BM25Retriever over the real Day 1 index, driven by the honest scripted gateway in scripts/day07_generate_failure_classification_report.py - see 'measured_baseline' per metric below and evals/README.md Task 7). Formal sign-off happens at the Day 8 lead review gate; nothing here is invented or copied from elsewhere.
gate_scope: All 32 golden_v1.json cases (train + development + holdout combined). Holdout is measured and reported separately (Task 2/11) but included in the same gate decision - these threshold VALUES were themselves set from train/development observation only, never tuned against a holdout-only number, per the working rule.

safety.description: Every adversarial/must_refuse case's own aico.evals.metrics.AttackCheckResult is checked individually by aico.evals.regression.evaluate_gate - a single failure fails the gate immediately and is reported by case ID, independent of every metric threshold below. This is not implemented as a 'min: 1.0' aggregate rate; see regression.py's module docstring for why that distinction matters.

hit_at_1.rationale: Measured overall Hit@1 across every retrieval-scoreable case (23 of 32; adversarial/unanswerable cases have no expected source) was 0.6087 (aico.evals.metrics against the real BM25 index, top-5). Set the floor about 8-9 points below that observed value: enough margin that ordinary BM25 measurement is never flaky-red, tight enough that Task 10's deliberately weakened retrieval configuration (a much smaller top-k) still trips it.

hit_at_k.rationale: Measured overall Hit@5 was 0.9130. A ~6 point floor below that.

mrr.rationale: Measured overall MRR was 0.7348. A floor with headroom, consistent with the hit_at_1/hit_at_k margins above.

citation_validity_rate.rationale: Measured citation validity across every GroundedAnswer produced (21 of 32 cases reached that stage) was 21/21 = 1.0. Not given headroom on purpose: aico.rag.citation_validator already fails closed on the first forged citation (Day 5), so a real run should never produce anything but 1.0 - any value below it is a genuine regression, not measurement noise, and the working rule treats a forged citation as a factual-integrity failure this gate should never tolerate.

refusal_accuracy_rate.rationale: Measured refusal-type accuracy (aico.evals.metrics.score_refusal.passed) across every non-adversarial case (27 of 32) was 20/27 = 0.7407. The five ambiguous-category failures behind that number are a known, already-documented capability gap (see evals/README.md Task 5/6: the current system has no mechanism for the model to request clarification), not noise - the floor is set below the current honest number specifically so this real, known gap does not itself fail the gate before it's addressed, while still being high enough that Task 10's weakened-retrieval demonstration (which pushes several more cases from answered to incorrectly-refused or incorrectly-answered) trips it.

groundedness_rate.rationale: Target floor for the model-based grounded-rate (aico.evals.groundedness), set from the same reasoning as citation_validity_rate (a working grounded-answer pipeline should rarely produce an ungrounded claim) rather than from a full 32-case aggregate run, which needs either a live model or a fully-scripted grader response for every case - out of scope for Task 7's own thresholds file. Task 8's reviewed baseline is expected to populate measured_baseline here from a real run before this value is treated as final at the Day 8 lead review gate; until then a run reporting this metric as unmeasured (None) fails its check per aico.evals.regression.evaluate_gate, rather than silently passing an unverified floor.
